reasoning_content:
Interesting — "no context exists with the name k3d-sch-local" yet the `&&` chain still printed "traefik disabled as expected"? Wait: `kubectl config use-context k3d-sch-local && kubectl wait ...` — if use-context fails, the chain should stop. But the last command `kubectl -n kube-system get deployment traefik >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo present || echo disabled` — that's a separate statement after `&&`... Let me re-read my command:

`kubectl config use-context k3d-sch-local && kubectl wait ... && kubectl get nodes -o wide && kubectl get storageclass && kubectl -n kube-system get deployment traefik ...`

All chained with &&. If the first fails, none of the subsequent ones should run. But "traefik disabled as expected" was printed... Actually wait, the output shows "traefik disabled as expected" first, then the error. Hmm, output order is strange. Actually the `||` at the end: `kubectl -n kube-system get deployment traefik >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "traefik present (unexpected)" || echo "traefik disabled as expected"`.

Hmm, but if use-context failed with "no context exists", how did anything else run? Unless... the error "no context exists" came from a different invocation. Actually wait — maybe the exit code 0 is because the last echo succeeded.

Let me think: the actual output lines:
```
traefik disabled as expected

error: no context exists with the name: "k3d-sch-local"
```

This ordering suggests: the chain ran, something printed "traefik disabled as expected", then an error appeared. Confusing. Maybe stdout/stderr interleaving. Actually it's possible that use-context failed, then `&&` short-circuited... no.

Wait, actually maybe `kubectl config use-context` printed nothing on success? No, it failed: "no context exists".

Hmm, unless the shell evaluated differently. Let me just check kubeconfig state directly.

action.command: echo "KUBECONFIG=${KUBECONFIG:-unset}"; kubectl config get-contexts 2>&1 | head; ls -la ~/.kube/config 2>&1; grep -A3 "name: k3d" ~/.kube/config 2>/dev/null | head -10
